subject: Mystic River Watershed Flooding and Resilience
overview: The committee hosted a regional presentation on climate adaptation and flood mitigation strategies for the Mystic River Watershed. Discussion focused on infrastructure projects, municipal solar initiatives, and social resiliency programs within Medford.

items.title: Committee and Webinar Introductions
items.summary: The webinar was introduced as a collaborative effort between the Medford Energy and Environment Committee and the Tufts Energy Group to discuss regional flood risks.

items.title: Resilient Mystic Collaborative Overview
items.summary: Julie Wormser presented on the voluntary partnership between 20 municipalities to manage climate challenges such as extreme rainfall, coastal flooding, and urban heat across the watershed.

items.title: Climate Risk and Social Resiliency Simulation
items.summary: The committee reviewed a simulated nor'easter exercise used to identify cascading infrastructure failures and their disproportionate impacts on low-income and non-English speaking residents.

items.title: Medford Departmental and Social Resiliency Updates
items.summary: Staff discussed the reorganization of the Office of Planning, Development and Sustainability and the city's innovative Community Liaison Program, which the state is now using as a model for vulnerability preparedness.

items.title: Stormwater and Renewable Energy Projects
items.summary: Staff reported on stormwater design grants for South Medford and progress on municipal solar projects, including a library array that covers the building's full electricity demand.

items.title: Carr Park Solar and Cooling Initiatives
items.summary: The city announced a $1.5 million federal earmark to fund a solar-powered basketball court cover at Carr Park to provide cooling and renewable energy for a nearby fire station.

items.title: Infrastructure and Urban Forestry Discussion
items.summary: The presentation concluded with details on storm hardening the Amelia Earhart Dam and collaborative tree-planting efforts to mitigate heat islands through the 'Trees Medford' program.
